# Review — ani-015-c

## Pass 1

Units are numbered from 0 in the order of `sentences`. All 43 units and 243 words were checked against the packet, the established file, conventions.md, the model and the published parts. Every word was also compared by script with every published word that has the same sign sequence: all of them agree in reading, roles, tr, lemmas and say. Words with new spellings were checked by hand against the published spellings of the same reading. I did not change any sign code or the order of the signs. After editing: the JSON loads; the concatenated sign sequence equals the established file's (831 glyphs); morph `g` covers every glyph of every word exactly once; no `s`/`t` fields; every det has an empty tr. The `ln` of every unit matches the line of its first established word. The `rubric` flags match the established file word for word (w0, w7, w8, w110, w193), and every unit with rubric words (U0, U1, U18, U34) says red in its note. The three restorations (U12 n, U21 the O29 in sꜥꜣ, U41 the first nb) carry `restored` on their glyphs, and each note says so. Joins and splits are all stated in the notes: ind | ḥr·k, di·k | tw (twice), rḫ | st, ms | sw, ḥr | r, iꜣw | n·k and ms·n | tw.

### Changes
- U41 (w227) · reading, say, glyph roles, morph, l, i, n · major · The note read ꜣḫw 'splendid' "with Budge (χu), the ibis left out", and its own text admitted that ḫwi 'protect' fits the signs as they stand (ḫ, arm, w, roll; no ibis). That is an emendation made without the formula, in a place where two readings are possible. Conventions: "Where more than one reading is possible, translate what stands and say so." · Changes: reading ḫw, say khu, lemma ꜣḫ → ḫwi (known; Spell 125 address), D36 det, l "(which-are)-protected(?)", i "which are protected(?) by your beauty". The note now gives the signs, the stative of ḫwi, and Budge's χu/ꜣḫw as the other possibility, and calls the reading doubtful.
- U25 (w146) · l, i, n, morph gloss · minor · l/i "may-be-joined / may I be joined" is Budge's passive ('may I be joined'). The form is an active sḏm·f with no tw, and the note itself calls it "a sḏm·f for a wish". Also, the known lemma smꜣ is 'to slay, kill', and the occurrence gloss did not keep the two words apart. · Changes: l "may-unite · I · with", i "may I unite with the noble and excellent spirits …". The note says the form is active and that this is not smꜣ 'slay'. Gloss: "to unite, join; with m, to unite with (verb; written with the lungs and windpipe; not smꜣ 'slay')". (The glosser should broaden smꜣ.)
- U42 (w234) · glyph tr, n · minor · G39 had tr ꜣ, and the note said "read ꜣ as in the hymn to Ra". The hymn to Ra and Spell 61 both code this duck as phon sꜣ and open their notes "The papyrus writes ḏ-f / ḏfsꜣ …; read ḏfꜣw". The formula here named only the doubled ḏf. · Changes: G39 tr sꜣ. The note now opens "The papyrus writes ḏfḏfsꜣ, the cobra and the viper twice and the pintail duck sꜣ where the vulture ꜣ is expected; read ḏfꜣw 'provisions', the usual partner of ḥw". The later sentence now says "standing for ꜣ as in the hymn to Ra and Spell 61".
- U0 · n · minor · The note said i 'O' is "the call that the previous part ended on". ani-015-b ends with ntk is wḏ n·i st nb·i, and this call opens the new part. · Now reads "the call that opens this part, right after the previous part's last words (ntk is wḏ n·i st nb·i)".
- U12 (w72) · n · minor · The note said "read ꜣb with Budge's āb", but Budge's ā is ꜥ (conventions), so his āb does not support ꜣb. The reading comes from the sign. · Now reads "read ꜣb, the chisel's value (Budge prints āb, with his ā, which is ꜥ, where the sign has ꜣ)".
- U13 · l, i · minor · The note calls ḥp·t's "verb and form doubtful", but l and i had a plain "hastening". · Now "hastening(?)" in both, as U22 already has.
- U5 (w32) · glyph role · style · In rwd, Z4 was coded phon y, but the note (and the reading rwd) say the two strokes are not read. · Z4 det, tr empty; the note adds "(coded as a classifier)".
- U8 · l · style · i had "may be reckoned(?)" but l had "may-be-reckoned" without the (?). · l "may-be-reckoned(?)".
- U28 · i · style · i added "to the west" as if it were in the text; l has only "to-the-right" (wnmy). · Now "to the right (that is, the west)".
- U32 (w185) · n · style · iwty was coded Aa13 phon iwt, and nothing in the note said why a flat-bar code carries iwt. · The note adds that the sign has the shape of the negative arms (D35) as printed in line 21 and is read so.
- U38 · l · style · "have-illumined" echoes Budge's "thou illuminest". · l "have-brightened", the same as sḥḏ 'brightens' in U36 and U39 (i already had "lit up").

### Refused
- U5 sqdt (say Seqedet) for the Sektet-bark, where every published part has sktt / Seketet. The signs are s, a sign coded Aa28 qd, and two hands. The note reads them from the signs, keeps the known lemma sktt, and says the shapes are uncertain. Changing the reading or say to Seketet would ignore the signs. Kept.
- U27 nwt written with the town sign O49. The note says it is used for its sounds and compares niwwt in U41. Nut written with a sound sign is not a sure slip, so the "papyrus writes" formula was not added. Kept.
- "The papyrus writes X; read Y" in U42: the sense allows only ḏfꜣw beside ḥw. Kept (now complete; see Changes). No other unit needed the formula. nḥḥ written ḥḥ (U24, U30) is the copy's usual spelling and is treated so in every published part.
- U4, U27, U40: the boat-like sign P1 read m, following Budge's mā. Its codes come from the established reader, the notes say what is printed, and U40 calls the reading doubtful. Kept.
- U7 smw, U9 sm / wn-rꜣ·f, U16 msms, U17 r-ꜥ, U22 ḥpyw and iwty with nothing after it, U37 ḥr ḏrt, U40 mhꜣyw, U41 ḏꜣḏꜣwt and pryt: each is called doubtful in its note, and l/i carry (?) where the sense is guessed. Kept.
- U14 ir·n·k and U22 ḥpyw: a w is coded phon and the note says it is not read. This is the house practice (015-b's E23 in šnꜥ·tw), so I kept it. U5's Z4 was different: two strokes with tr y are not a sound sign, and I changed it.
- U32 di·i tw 'I have placed you', a sḏm·f with past sense: it is possible, it agrees with Budge's tense, and the note labels it. A present tense ('I place you') would also fit. Kept.
- U11 iw·f r šm·f with ·f after the infinitive: the note explains it as a future that repeats the subject, and the doubt about who 'he' is is stated. Kept.
- U2 "every face is watching you", U35 "rises like gold", U13 "in one brief moment": these coincide with Budge only because they are the literal words (ḥr + infinitive, m nbw, ꜣt šrit). Kept.
- p placement: U1 (Ani's speech), U19 (what he says after U18's say-line) and U35 (the new address after U34). U0, U18 and U34 are say-lines without p, as in 015-b's U25. Kept.
- Occurrence glosses on smw, sm, imw, itrw, ḏꜣḏꜣt, pr and ḥw were kept. Each separates this word from a different known sense (smw 'herbs', sm 'go', ḥw the god Hu, and so on). Moving them into the glossary is the glosser's job: smꜣ, sm, smw, ḥw and pr need `__broaden__`.
- Budge-isms: none in l/i after the U25 and U38 changes. I checked thee/thou/thy/saith/homage/triumph/glorious/stablished/victorious/behold/beatified/illumine/exult/progress/eventide/statutes. House renderings agree: "the Osiris (the scribe) Ani", "true of voice", Nu, Nut, Ra, Maat, "Your Majesty", the Disk, the Two Lands, the necropolis.

## Pass 2

This was a fresh full re-read of all 43 units, numbered as in Pass 1, and of every entry in gloss.json. Sign codes and order were untouched. After editing: both files load; the sign sequence equals the established file's (831 glyphs); morph `g` covers every glyph of every word exactly once; there are no `s`/`t` fields and no det has a tr. The gloss key set equals exactly the lemmas used minus the known-lemmas keys (16 entries: ḫꜣst, pwnt, kt, ḥpi, ḥfn, šri, km, msms, ntꜥ, rꜣ-ꜥ, sꜥꜣ, wnmy, mhꜣw, ḥbbt, sḥb, wṯs). Every `__broaden__` key is a known lemma that the units use, and each value begins with the known entry whole + " · ". The pass-1 change to ḫwi needs no gloss work: ḫwi is known ("to protect, guard, keep safe"), and ꜣḫ is still used in U25.

### Changes — gloss.json
- __broaden__ smꜣ · minor · The entry carried "(passive) to be joined", which is Budge's rendering and was dropped from U25 in Pass 1. It also called the verb "a second sense" of 'slay', though it is a different word · Now "· a second word of the same spelling: to unite, join; with m, to unite with (verb; written with the lungs and windpipe; Budge: sama)".
- __broaden__ (new) nṯri · minor · The known entry has only the verb 'be divine'. U33 uses nṯry as an adjective with r for the comparative, and nothing covered that · Added "· also nṯry, divine (adjective, nisba of nṯr; with r, 'more divine than'; Budge: neteri)".
- __broaden__ (new) wꜥ · minor · The known entry has only 'one; someone'. U9's wꜥ·ṯi is the stative 'being alone', which was uncovered · Added "· also to be one, be alone (verb; the stative 'alone, by oneself'; Budge: uā)".
- ḥfn · minor · The Budge spelling "ḥefenu" is not in the packet, which has ḥefnu (w82). "plural ḥfnw" and "noun m." were also pinned to this one writing · Now "a hundred thousand (numeral; written with the tadpole; Budge: ḥefnu)".
- wṯs · minor · The Budge spelling "uθes" is not in the packet, which has uθesu (w230). "participle 'who lifts up'" was pinned to U42 · Now "(verb; Budge: uθesu, 'supporting')".
- msms · minor · The Budge spelling "mes-mes" is the note's hyphenation; the packet has mesmes (w92). "written with the legs as classifier" described this passage's spelling · Now "to pass through (?) (reduplicated verb; reading and sense doubtful; Budge: mesmes, 'count')".
- wnmy · minor · "right hand, taken as the west" called the word a noun and pinned the sense to U28 · Now a nisba adjective, also used as a noun, 'the right side', with the general reason it means the west (the right hand of one who faces south).
- __broaden__ ḥw · style · "often paired with ḏfꜣw" was given without Budge's form · Now "food, plenty (noun m.; paired with ḏfꜣw 'provisions'; Budge: ḥu, 'meats')". The occurrence gloss in U42 was brought into line.
- ḥpi · style · "the form and sense are doubtful" spoke of this passage's forms · Now "(verb of motion; sense doubtful; …)". Both Budge forms are kept (packet w77, w127).
- mhꜣw · style · "the word and its first sign are doubtful" was about this print · Now "(noun, collective; reading doubtful; …)".
- kt · style · "of a moment or day, 'brief'" was U12's context · Cut.
- pwnt · style · "in the east where the sun rises" was this hymn's reason for naming Punt, not part of the name · Cut. Now "the land of incense, on the Red Sea coast".
- __broaden__ smw, sm, imw · style · These entries described this passage's sign or Budge's "(?)" ("reading of the sign doubtful", "read with Budge", "written with the sun's rays as classifier") · Each now gives only the sense, "(?)", "doubtful" and Budge's form.

### Changes — units.json
- U29, U31 (ḥtp·k) · glyph role · style · R4 was coded phon here and log in U0, U1 and U14, all with the same spelling. The house uses both codings, but the part should be consistent · Changed to log.
- U8 (tꜣw) · glyph role · style · The first N16 was coded phon, while U16's tꜣ and U36's tꜣwy have it as log · Changed to log.

### Refused
- ḫꜣst "Budge: set": an odd reading for the hill-country sign, but it is what the packet prints (w51). Kept.
- km 'to complete' (Budge qam), ntꜥ, rꜣ-ꜥ, sꜥꜣ, sḥb, šri, ḥbbt: general, and their Budge spellings match the packet. The (?) on rꜣ-ꜥ is the lemma's own doubt. Kept.
- itrw broaden ("the river-length, a measure of long distances"): it is a general sense of the word. Kept.
- Occurrence glosses on smw, sm, imw, itrw, smꜣ, ḏꜣḏꜣt and pr stay. They name this occurrence's sense among several, and they agree with the glossary.
- ꜣbw (U12) needs no broaden: the known ꜣb entry already covers the noun (n ꜣbw).
- sip 'inspect, examine' for 'reckon' (U8), sš 'paint, writing' (U8), ḥḏ 'be bright' (U16 ḥḏ-tꜣ), dwꜣw 'morning' (U20), wn and rꜣ (U9): the known entries cover these uses. No broaden.
- Units re-read: no further issues in readings, grammar labels, l/i, Budge-isms, names, rubrics, restorations, ln or p beyond the above. The pass-1 refusals stand.
